name: Question 7
problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R$ and its subset $F={A\in {\text{M}}_{2}(R)\,|\,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]A=A[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]}.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $F$ is closed under matrix addition
- $F$ is closed under scalar multiplication
- $F$ is a subspace of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
- $F$ is **not** a subspace of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
worked_solution:
Recall that a subset of a vector space is a subspace if it's closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. If ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}$ are two matrices from $F,$ then ${A}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]{A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]{A}_{2}.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}({A}_{1}+{A}_{2})[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] & ={A}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]+{A}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]{A}_{1}+[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]{A}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]({A}_{1}+{A}_{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${A}_{1}+{A}_{2}$ is a matrix from $F.$ So, $F$ is closed under addition.

- Statement II is true. If $A$ is an element of $F,$ then $A[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]A.$ For $k\in R,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(kA)[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] & =k\cdot A[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =k[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}](kA).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $kA$ is a matrix from $F.$ So, $F$ is closed under scalar multiplication.

- Statement III is true, while statement IV is false. $F$ is a subspace because it's closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III only."

  • Statement I is true. If A1 and A2 are two matrices from F, then A1[1−123]=[1−123]A1 and A2[1−123]=[1−123]A2. So, we have (A1+A2)[1−123]=A1[1−123]+A2[1−123]=[1−123]A1+[1−123]A2=[1−123](A1+A2). Therefore, A1+A2 is a matrix from F. So, F is closed under addition.

  • Statement II is true. If A is an element of F, then A[1−123]=[1−123]A. For k∈R, we get
    (kA)[1−123]=k⋅A[1−123]=k[1−123]A=[1−123](kA). Therefore, kA is a matrix from F. So, F is closed under scalar multiplication.

  • Statement III is true, while statement IV is false. F is a subspace because it's closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
